newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drug chief defends Mexican counterparts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug chief defends Mexican counterparts.

text.p: U.S. drug czar Gen. Barry McCaffrey defended on Friday his embattled Mexican counterparts, who he said are limited from cooperating with the United States by nationalistic attitudes.
McCaffrey made a quick visit to Mexico on Wednesday to meet with President Ernesto Zedillo after his Mexican counterpart was charged last month with taking bribes from a drug cartel.

"On the other side of the fence, there is an intense nationalistic debate, a crescendo of disapproval and antipathy toward the United States, isolating and constraining what we say are these incredibly brave Mexican patriots in charge in their own country and limiting their options to cooperate with the United States," McCaffrey told reporters. "There's a problem on both sides of the border with that."
McCaffrey was in Boston to receive Harvard Medical School's Norman Zinberg award, given annually to identify advances in the field of addiction medicine.

McCaffrey declined to comment on a Time magazine report that Mexico would scrap its current anti-drug agency, the National Institute for Combatting Drugs (INCD), and replace it with another modeled after the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).

The INCD has come under fire after its chief, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, McCaffrey's counterpart, was arrested for allegedly taking bribes from the country's top drug kingpin, Amado Carillo Fuentes.
McCaffrey said the drug trade through Mexico is having an "atrocious" impact there, resulting in corruption and violence, including the assassination of police officers and prosecutors.

"There's a (economic and political) revolution going on in Mexico, and all of this has as its backdrop $30 billion worth of the corrupting influence of U.S. drug dollars spent in this country," he said.
